title: Healthy Banana Fritters (Sugar Free)
description: These healthy added sugar free banana fritters are gluten free, naturally sweetened, and taste like banana bread in fritter form. They are baked, not fried and made with better for you ingredients.

hero.alt: Golden baked banana fritters on parchment paper drizzled with white icing and topped with caramelised banana slices

thumbnail.alt: A spoon drizzling white icing over golden baked banana fritters topped with caramelised banana slices on parchment paper

instructions.text: Add the bananas to a bowl and mash well, then mix in the cinnamon.
Crack in the egg and pour in the melted coconut oil. Mix until combined.
Add the dry ingredients: oats, almond flour, oat flour and baking powder. Mix until combined.
Spoon a heaped tablespoon of batter onto a lined baking tray (approx 5 fritters). Optionally top with a few slices of banana.
Bake for 23 to 25 minutes or until edges are golden brown.

notes: Use gram measurements for best accuracy and texture.
The riper the bananas, the sweeter and more flavourful the fritters will be.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Reheat in the oven or air fryer to restore texture.
Optional toppings: sliced bananas, a drizzle of maple syrup, or powdered monkfruit and water icing.

story.subtitle: Sugar Free & Gluten Free
paragraphs: if you tried my viral sugar free apple fritters, you are going to love this banana bread version. these healthy banana fritters are naturally sweetened, gluten free, and taste like banana bread in cozy fritter form. they're golden on the outside, soft on the inside, and packed with warm cinnamon flavour. all the deliciousness of banana bread but without any of the hassle, and completely added sugar free, but you can always drizzle your fave sweetener on top too!

this is not a traditional banana fritter recipe. these banana bread fritters are baked instead of fried, have minimal oil and are a much lighter and healthier alternative but still give off the same vibe.

the batter technique here is super simple, you just need one bowl: mash the bananas well first as your base, mix in the egg and coconut oil, then fold in the dry ingredients last and only mix until just combined. overworking it once the oats and flour go in is what makes fritters dense rather than moist. the batter should be the consistency of a thick pancake mix.

because they're sweetened entirely with overripe bananas, these fritters have that natural sweetness without any added sugar. as bananas ripen and develop those dark brown spots, their natural starches convert to sugars, making them perfect for baking without any need for sweetener. that means the banana ripeness matters a lot here. opt for overripe bananas for the best result as you truly won't feel the lack of added sugars. they'll also produce a more flavourful fritter, and since the bananas are doing both the sweetening and are responsible for the actual taste of the fritters, it does make a difference. this is a great recipe for those bananas that have been sitting on your counter a day too long and are too mushy to eat on their own but you don't want them to go to waste.

apart from the bananas, the dry ingredients in this batter are giving these fritters a lot of structure while keeping them moist. the combination of porridge oats, almond flour, and oat flour gives these fritters a slightly hearty texture that sits somewhere between a traditional fritter and a banana bread muffin top. the oats add a gentle chewiness and natural fibre, while the almond flour contributes healthy fats that help keep you feeling satisfied and extra moisture.

these banana fritters are ideal for breakfast, meal prep, or a healthy sweet snack when you want something comforting but not overly indulgent. they also reheat beautifully in the oven or air fryer, making them great for batch baking on the weekend.

you can top them with banana slices before baking for a cuter and more caramelised result, or finish with a simple icing drizzle made from powdered monkfruit sweetener and water, an extra dusting of cinnamon and a dollop of yogurt. or to make them more indulgent, they taste divine served still warm with a scoop of your favourite ice cream. the fact that they're added sugar free means it's not sickly with ice cream but it does add an extra touch of decadence!

storage wise: these fritters keep well in an airtight container in the fridge or counter depending on the room temp for up to 3 days. they reheat really well in the oven at 160°C for 5 to 8 minutes or in the air fryer for a few minutes. they also freeze well individually: allow the banana fritters to cool completely, transfer to your freezer bag or method of choice, then pop in the freezer. reheat them individually from frozen in the oven or air fryer. honestly, since the recipe is small batch, they don't normally last long enough for storage lol, and any banana baked good never tastes as good as it does freshly baked!

faq.question: Are these healthy banana fritters completely sugar free?
faq.answer: These banana fritters are made without added or refined sugar. They are naturally sweetened with ripe bananas, which contain naturally occurring fruit sugars. For extra sweetness, optional toppings like maple syrup or a powdered sweetener drizzle can be added, but the base recipe is completely added sugar free.

faq.question: Are these banana fritters gluten free?
faq.answer: Yes, these healthy banana fritters are gluten free as long as you use certified gluten free oats and oat flour. Oats are naturally gluten free but can be cross-contaminated during processing, so always check packaging if you are strictly gluten free or have coeliac disease.

faq.question: Why are my banana fritters not sweet enough?
faq.answer: The sweetness of these banana fritters depends almost entirely on how ripe your bananas are. Use very overripe bananas with lots of brown spots for the best natural sweetness. If your bananas were still quite yellow, the fritters will taste less sweet. You can fix this easily by adding a drizzle of maple syrup on top or mixing a little sweetener of your choice into the batter before baking.

faq.question: How do I store healthy banana fritters?
faq.answer: Store banana fritters in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. For the best eating experience, reheat them in the oven at around 160°C for 5 minutes or pop them in the air fryer for 3 to 4 minutes to restore their soft interior and lightly golden edges. They are also fine eaten cold.

faq.question: Why are these banana fritters baked instead of fried?
faq.answer: These banana fritters are baked instead of fried to keep them lighter, less oily, and easier to make at home without the need for a deep fryer or large amounts of oil. They're not identical to traditional deep-fried fritters in texture, but they're very similar in flavour profile and that warm, golden banana bread character. Baking also means the whole batch comes out at once rather than frying in small batches.

faq.question: Can I freeze banana fritters?
faq.answer: Yes. Let them cool completely first, then freeze in a single layer on a tray before transferring to an airtight container or zip-lock bag. They keep in the freezer for up to 2 months. Reheat directly from frozen in the oven or air fryer until warmed through and the edges are golden again.

faq.question: Can I make these banana fritters dairy free?
faq.answer: Yes, this recipe is naturally dairy free. The only fat used is coconut oil, which is completely plant-based. If you want to make a dairy-free icing to drizzle on top, simply mix powdered monkfruit sweetener or icing sugar with a small amount of plant-based milk or water until you reach a drizzleable consistency.

tips: Use gram measurements for accuracy. Cup measurements can vary a lot depending on how tightly ingredients are packed, and this recipe works best when the ratios are precise.
Mash or blend the bananas very well to avoid lumps in the batter. A smooth banana base gives a more uniform fritter texture.
Bake until lightly golden on the edges but still soft in the centre. Overbaking can dry them out. They will firm up slightly as they cool.
For a prettier finish, top each fritter with a thin banana slice before baking. The banana caramelises slightly in the oven and looks gorgeous with an icing drizzle on top.

alternatives: Avocado oil or another neutral oil
More oat flour (same quantity works well)
Certified gluten free oats (for strict gluten free)
